title: Mirror an uncertain Engram turn-begin outcome durably when a delegation child is canceled or fails
outcome: Found by Codex /review-code on tm-cr0i round 3 and verified in source. When a child delegation is canceled (or fails) while a turn_begin is in flight: Stop skips the checkpoint because the local grant mirror is still None; settle_terminal_delegation_child_locked -> clear_delegation_child_queue_locked (src/delegations.rs:3492-3501) discards the child's queued prompts and with them any durable queued intent / begun_grant_id marker; the superseded-begin path (src/engram_host_adapter.rs ~4217-4252) fires its compensating turn_checkpoint with let _ = and on failure only sets rebind_required, never mirroring the grant into active_grant_id. A crash in that window leaves: delegation Failed/Canceled persisted, active_grant_id None, no queued intent, routing token present - while Engram still has the grant begun. Today only eager boot recovery reconciles this (token -> session_status -> open_grant_id -> turn_checkpoint). The control fixture models Engram refusing a fresh session_bind while a grant is begun (invalid_control_session), so losing the token or skipping recovery would strand the child. tm-cr0i therefore skips only Completed children at boot and keeps Failed/Canceled eager. Fix direction: persist a durable uncertain-begin marker (or mirror the grant id) on the session record at cancellation/failure and when the compensating checkpoint fails, so local state is trustworthy; then extend the tm-cr0i skip to failed/canceled children and add a regression: cancel during begin, restart before settlement, assert the grant is checkpointed.
